primary_thesis: The live selective scan did not compute the specified Mamba recurrence (rel-max-err 0.92 at the measured init Delta=0.705); the same class of defect lives in the mLSTM TFLA term (0.882). MEASURED at 12K steps (M7): fixing the defect on the existing Mamba-1 (A1) gives -16.0% val PPL; migrating to Mamba-2/3 SSD (A2, d_state 128, +0.26% params) gives -13.8% at 1.94x the speed, and the two are not significantly apart -- the headline is the defect, not the architecture; what SSD buys is the cost of being correct (the exact operator is 19 MB in scalar-A form vs 19.3 GB in Mamba-1's). Version 2 re-screens A2 with the mLSTM recurrence corrected as well (A2x), then runs the winner through the identical pipeline both incumbents went through (Stage-0 -> 13D tower reused -> decoder x 3 seeds -> beam-3 official test split -> CheXbert -> paired bootstraps) and judges it against the 3-seed bands with a pre-registered claim rule. 'Indistinguishable across 3 seeds' is the expected and reportable outcome.
